experiments.question: Which pregame minutes forecast (conditional on playing) is most accurate?
experiments.hypothesis: Role/rotation features and gradient boosting beat a shrunk EWMA (the incumbent's EWM-5 analogue).
experiments.method: Ladder A-F walk-forward by season; OLS/stack weights fitted on 2016-17..2021-22 only; LightGBM refit each season on the previous five; empirical residual distribution fitted on development.
experiments.data: Played player-games, regular season; validation 2022-23..2023-24, holdout 2024-25..2025-26.
experiments.result: Validation MAE: A 5.61, B 5.20, C 5.02, D 4.99, E 4.84, F 4.85; E vs B -0.355 (95% CI -0.382 to -0.327) min. Holdout E MAE 4.76 (vs B -0.332 (95% CI -0.357 to -0.305)); incumbent sim MAE 6.17, bias -2.42 (E vs incumbent -1.427 (95% CI -1.482 to -1.377)).
experiments.interpretation: Each rung adds real accuracy; the incumbent's rotation simulator under-projects minutes for players who play by more than 2 minutes, which propagates into every counting stat.

experiments.question: Can a participation hurdle predict who plays without an injury report?
experiments.hypothesis: A LightGBM classifier on recent participation, days since last game and return-from-absence beats the EWMA participation rate and the incumbent's availability proxy.
experiments.method: Candidate pool = players who played for the team in its previous 10 games (absent rows added); classifier walk-forward by season; unconditional minutes = P(play) x E[min | play].
experiments.result: Validation Brier 0.1207 vs EWMA rate 0.1604 (incumbent 0.1684 vs ours 0.1162 on its rows); ECE 0.0043. Unconditional minutes MAE 5.79 vs 7.28 (EWMA) and incumbent 6.77 vs ours 6.01 (-0.755 (95% CI -0.799 to -0.712)). Holdout: Brier 0.1252, MAE 5.97, incumbent diff -0.837 (95% CI -0.881 to -0.795); 80% coverage of the hurdle mixture 0.805.
experiments.interpretation: Most DNPs are predictable from recent participation patterns; the rest needs the injury report.

experiments.question: Do teammate absences (injury report) improve minutes forecasts, and does the retrospective proxy transfer to the real point-in-time report?
experiments.hypothesis: Minutes freed by absent teammates are redistributed predictably (by position and usage).
experiments.method: E_inj adds out_min / out_new_min / out_pos_min / out_usage computed from who is absent from the box (proxy for the report). On 2025-26 the same model is scored with features built from the archived T-60 official injury report (OUT/DOUBTFUL).
experiments.data: Validation/holdout played rows; 2025-26 archived official injury reports (1,320 games).
experiments.result: Validation E_inj vs E -0.225 (95% CI -0.244 to -0.205) min MAE; holdout -0.217 (95% CI -0.237 to -0.197). 2025-26 with PIT report inputs: MAE 4.559 vs 4.755 without injury info (-0.196 (95% CI -0.224 to -0.171)) and 4.548 with the proxy (PIT vs proxy +0.011 (95% CI -0.001 to +0.024)); proxy/PIT out-minutes correlation 0.902.
experiments.interpretation: Teammate availability is the largest single pregame improvement available; the real T-60 report recovers most of the proxy's gain, so the gain is not a leakage artefact.

experiments.question: How much would knowing the starting lineup add?
experiments.hypothesis: Starter status explains a material share of remaining minutes error.
experiments.method: Oracle: E_inj + the actual starter flag (not pregame-knowable historically; lineups are announced ~30 min before tip and were never archived).
experiments.result: Oracle vs E_inj: validation -0.164 (95% CI -0.177 to -0.150), holdout -0.169 (95% CI -0.183 to -0.154) min MAE.
experiments.interpretation: Upper bound of a confirmed-lineup feed: worth capturing prospectively, smaller than the injury report.

experiments.question: Does forcing each team's expected minutes to sum to 240 (+OT) improve player minutes?
experiments.hypothesis: Team-level consistency (the incumbent's water-filling idea) removes errors.
experiments.method: Scale E[min | play] so that sum(P(play) x E[min|play]) = 241.5 per team-game; paired MAE.
experiments.result: Development +0.004 (95% CI -0.001 to +0.011); validation +0.009 (95% CI -0.003 to +0.019) min MAE (normalised minus raw).
experiments.interpretation: Hard budget constraints move minutes toward players whose uncertainty is not team-level.

experiments.question: Which model best projects points (conditional on playing)?
experiments.hypothesis: Minutes x shrunk per-minute rate with opponent/pace adjustment and boosting beats averages and the incumbent simulator.
experiments.method: Ladder A-F, NB2 (dispersion binned by mean) for every rung; best rung by validation CRPS, then its distribution family chosen by validation log score.
experiments.result: Validation CRPS A 3.325; B 3.272; C 3.181; D 3.175; E 3.159; F 3.167. Best E (empirical): CRPS 3.159, MAE 4.519, vs A -0.166 (95% CI -0.177 to -0.155), vs incumbent -0.330 (95% CI -0.348 to -0.314) (incumbent CRPS 3.527, bias -1.243). Holdout CRPS 3.166, vs A -0.175 (95% CI -0.187 to -0.165), vs incumbent -0.383 (95% CI -0.401 to -0.366).
experiments.interpretation: See RESULTS_NBA.md per-family table.

experiments.question: Does an opponent (position-specific, schedule-relative) and pace adjustment improve points?
experiments.hypothesis: Defences allow systematically different production to guards/forwards/centres than expected.
experiments.method: D = C x factor^beta x pace^beta_pace; factor = shrunk EWMA of actual/expected allowed by the opponent to the position (k=10 games); beta=0.663, beta_pace=0.257 fitted on development.
experiments.result: D vs C CRPS: validation -0.0052 (95% CI -0.0072 to -0.0030), holdout -0.0084 (95% CI -0.0105 to -0.0064); factor sd 0.031.
experiments.interpretation: Opponent effects are real but small relative to minutes and role.

experiments.question: Which outcome distribution is best calibrated for points, and does propagating minutes uncertainty help?
experiments.hypothesis: A mixture over minutes scenarios of NB(rate x minutes) is better calibrated than a single NB at the mean minutes (which ignores minutes risk).
experiments.method: Poisson / NB2 binned / discretised normal / empirical ratio (quantile mapping) / minutes mixture / single-minutes NB; parameters from development; validation log score, CRPS, PIT, rungs.
experiments.result: poisson: logS 3.6528, CRPS 3.3815, cover80 0.502, PITvar 1.690, rung Brier 0.09203; nb: logS 3.0191, CRPS 3.1641, cover80 0.765, PITvar 1.089, rung Brier 0.08767; normal: logS 3.0022, CRPS 3.1795, cover80 0.785, PITvar 1.028, rung Brier 0.08773; empirical: logS 2.9928, CRPS 3.1587, cover80 0.799, PITvar 1.002, rung Brier 0.08763; mixture: logS 3.0559, CRPS 3.1831, cover80 0.724, PITvar 1.178, rung Brier 0.08785; single_minutes_nb: logS 3.2289, CRPS 3.2430, cover80 0.637, PITvar 1.371, rung Brier 0.08842
experiments.interpretation: Chosen: empirical. The single-minutes NB is the overconfident case (PIT variance > 1); minutes uncertainty must be propagated.

experiments.question: Does teammate-absence information (usage freed) improve points?
experiments.hypothesis: Absent teammates' usage is redistributed to those who play.
experiments.method: E_inj (LightGBM + teammate absence proxy features) vs the best pregame model, validation CRPS.
experiments.data: Validation played rows (proxy = absence from the box; PIT version only for 2025-26).
experiments.result: E_inj minus best: -0.0542 (95% CI -0.0606 to -0.0484) CRPS.
experiments.interpretation: Injury-informed projections need the live report; the effect is measured with a retrospective proxy and confirmed for minutes on 2025-26 PIT reports.

experiments.question: Does a pace x efficiency model with schedule-adjusted ratings beat team scoring averages?
experiments.hypothesis: Opponent defence and pace explain team points beyond the team's own average.
experiments.method: Ridge off/def ratings for pace and points per 100 (refit weekly on earlier blocks, prior-season decay 0.35, 120-day half-life); D adds rest/back-to-back terms fitted on development.
experiments.result: Validation MAE/CRPS: A 9.67/6.844; B 9.59/6.790; C 9.44/6.664; D 9.41/6.641. Holdout best D_ratings_plus_rest: MAE 9.46, CRPS 6.698, vs A -0.339 (95% CI -0.420 to -0.251).
experiments.interpretation: Opponent strength and pace matter for team totals far more than for individual props.

experiments.question: Do player point projections reconcile with team points?
experiments.hypothesis: Sum over the candidate pool of P(play) x E[pts|play] matches the team model within 15%.
experiments.method: pf_core.gate.team_reconciliation per team-game (REVIEW > 15%, BLOCK > 35%).
experiments.result: Validation ratio mean 1.000 (5-95% [0.8827, 1.1183]), statuses {'PASS': 4730, 'REVIEW': 191, 'BLOCK': 1}; MAE player-sum 10.52 vs team model 9.41, 50/50 blend 9.43.
experiments.interpretation: Player and team projections are mutually consistent; the bottom-up sum carries extra information from player availability.

experiments.question: How much does the archived official injury report add to participation and unconditional minutes?
experiments.hypothesis: Report status (OUT/DOUBTFUL/QUESTIONABLE) sharply separates who plays.
experiments.method: Logistic recalibration of the hurdle logit + status dummies fitted on 2025-26 games before 2026-01-15, scored on later games (chronological, within the holdout season; nothing else tuned).
experiments.result: Brier 0.1320 -> 0.0868 (-0.0452 (95% CI -0.0486 to -0.0416)); unconditional minutes MAE 6.271 -> 4.701 (-1.570 (95% CI -1.665 to -1.471)). OUT/DOUBTFUL precision for absence 0.816, recall 0.743.
experiments.interpretation: The injury report is the decisive participation input; the forward projector uses it.

opponent_adjustment.summary: Position-specific opponent factors (defence's EWMA of actual/expected allowed to G/F/C, shrunk toward 1) plus an expected-pace factor, elasticities fitted on development. D improves on C in validation CRPS for 6 of 6 families; effects are small (factor sd ~0.02-0.06) next to minutes. Team-level: schedule-adjusted ridge ratings drive the team-points model.

opportunity.summary: Minutes is the dominant driver. Best pregame minutes model E (LightGBM): validation MAE 4.84 vs EWMA 5.20 vs incumbent 6.06 (bias -2.31); holdout 4.76 vs incumbent 6.17. Participation hurdle Brier 0.125 (holdout) vs 0.174 for the incumbent. Teammate-absence information is the largest further gain; the archived 2025-26 report confirms it pregame.

calibration.summary: Distributions are fitted on development residuals and frozen. Randomised-PIT coverage and PIT variance are reported per family; a single NB at the mean minutes is overconfident, the minutes mixture / binned NB are close to nominal. Threshold Brier at Kalshi-like rungs is reported on the same rows as the incumbent.

failed_experiments.name: NBA-MIN-05: Does forcing each team's expected minutes to sum to 240 (+OT) improve player minutes?
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: Development +0.004 (95% CI -0.001 to +0.011); validation +0.009 (95% CI -0.003 to +0.019) min MAE (normalised minus raw).
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Hard budget constraints move minutes toward players whose uncertainty is not team-level.

failed_experiments.name: Blowout risk via linear context terms (D vs C) on high expected-margin games
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: D vs C on rows with |expected margin| >= 9: -0.022 (95% CI -0.049 to +0.005) min MAE (no reliable gain); blowouts are not over-represented among big misses (lift 1.02) but carry bias +1.30.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Rating-based expected margin is too weak a blowout signal; a real pregame spread history is needed before modelling garbage time explicitly.

failed_experiments.name: points: minutes-scenario mixture with a single within-minutes NB dispersion
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: PIT variance ratio 1.178, cover80 0.724: still too narrow for scoring families (shooting variance is not NB-like given minutes); the empirical/binned-NB marginal fits are better calibrated.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Use mixtures only where validated (rebounds, assists, threes, FGA).

failed_experiments.name: Process: two silent numerical failures caught before results were frozen
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: (1) a pandas all-NaN groupby sum returns 0, which turned opponent factors into inf at the 2016-17 opener; (2) pf_core.models.fit_opponent_beta returns its first golden-section probe (0.4549) when any base mean is NaN, which made every family's beta identical. Both fixed (explicit counts; finite development mask).
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Any fitted scalar equal across families, or equal to an optimiser probe, is treated as a defect until explained.
